edition.title: Edition / Close reading
edition.summary: Close reading of the De Michelis reconstruction and provisional witness projections.
details: Text selector switches between De Michelis and the provisional witness projections.
Structure uses each view’s own protocol divisions; canonical loci sit underneath and are witness-independent.
The right inspector separates textual structure, provisional K provenance, historical source notes, De Michelis apparatus, named entities, and researcher annotations.
The K/A1/A2/N/B texts are not documentary transcriptions. They are apparatus-derived scaffolding and must not be cited as if they were the printed witnesses.

anatomy.title: Protocol anatomy
anatomy.summary: A navigation aid that divides a protocol into internal blocks.
details: Where De Michelis marks Joly-source loci they may help delimit blocks; elsewhere neutral sentence groups are used.
This is not an interpretation of authorship or a claim about historical compositional layers.
The layer can be revised without changing canonical locus IDs.

provenance.title: K provenance
provenance.summary: Local comparison of the De Michelis reconstruction with the provisional K projection.
details: K-attested means the aligned provisional K text agrees locally.
Supplied / not in K means De Michelis contains material absent from the temporary K projection.
Differs from K means both contain text but the readings differ.
This layer will be recalculated from the documentary Znamja transcription when that witness is ingested.

source-notes.title: Historical source notes
source-notes.summary: Notes marked by historical asterisks that belong to the textual tradition rather than to De Michelis’s modern apparatus.
details: The marker stays at its exact position in the running text.
The note body is stored separately and can be opened from the marker.
In the present De Michelis appendix two unambiguous historical asterisk notes were identified in Protocol II.
Documentary witnesses will later verify their exact wording and distribution.

apparatus.title: De Michelis critical apparatus
apparatus.summary: Numbered notes recording readings and omissions across the editions used by De Michelis.
details: This is preserved as scholarly evidence and provenance.
It is not the final project collation.
Once documentary witnesses are ingested, direct comparison of those witnesses will become primary and this apparatus will remain a reference layer.

entities.title: Named entities
entities.summary: Indexed people, places, organizations, and works linked to occurrences in the current text views.
details: The index is a research aid, not a definitive authority file.
Counts for provisional witnesses inherit the limitations of those apparatus-derived texts.
Entities will be recomputed for documentary transcriptions.

annotations.title: Research annotations
annotations.summary: Interpretive annotations created by the researcher and deliberately separated from transcription and apparatus.
details: Annotations are stored locally in the browser until exported.
They may contain hypotheses such as economic discourse, editorial voice, or a possible Sharapov/Boutmy parallel.
They are not documentary facts and are not automatically committed to canonical TEI.
Use JSON or TEI export for preservation and review.

synopsis.title: Synopsis / Compare
synopsis.summary: Configurable comparison across witness views using non-parallel structures.
details: Choose an organizing witness/structure and reorder visible witnesses.
Differences are generated from the current text layers.
Because K/A1/A2/N/B are currently provisional apparatus-derived reconstructions, the synopsis is a tool-building preview rather than the final collation.
The interface is designed so documentary witnesses can replace the provisional layers without redesigning the synopsis.

tradition.title: Tradition / transmission model
tradition.summary: A visualization of textual relationships, not a settled stemma of the project.
details: The current graph represents the De Michelis model as a working hypothesis.
The architecture supports additional, versioned transmission hypotheses, including a future model formulated by the research team.
Solid-looking graphical links should not be read as newly established historical facts.

search.title: Search
search.summary: Full-text search across the De Michelis reconstruction and current witness projections.
details: Search results are linked back to close reading.
Witness-specific results currently reflect the provisional reconstructed witness text.
Search will automatically become more reliable when documentary transcriptions replace those projections.

index.title: Index
index.summary: Authority-style browser for people, places, organizations, and works.
details: Each entry links to current occurrences.
Forms and counts may require correction as the corpus grows.
The index is designed to survive witness replacement because entity IDs are separate from witness text IDs.

distant.title: Distant reading
distant.summary: Exploratory aggregate views: entity atlas, witness fingerprints, geography, co-occurrence, concepts, and variation density.
details: These visualizations are exploratory research tools, not arguments or conclusions.
Any witness comparison is currently constrained by apparatus-derived witness projections.
The same views can later be recomputed from documentary witnesses without changing the interface.

loci.title: Canonical loci
loci.summary: Stable witness-independent anchors used to connect non-parallel textual structures.
details: A locus is not a protocol number.
Protocol divisions may differ across witnesses while the canonical locus identifier remains stable.
Current mappings are provisional and can be refined when documentary witnesses are aligned.
Stable locus IDs are the main mechanism that allows future witnesses to be inserted without rebuilding the system.

research.title: Research workspace
research.summary: Workspace for canonical loci and local-first interpretive annotations.
details: Use the locus browser to inspect cross-witness structural mappings.
Use annotations for hypotheses and research notes, not for corrections to documentary transcription.
Repository-level persistence is not implemented yet; export annotations before moving browsers or clearing local data.

method.title: Method
method.summary: Editorial principles, architecture notes, downloads, and project documentation.
details: This page should be the first place to check what is documentary, reconstructed, provisional, experimental, or planned.
Version 2.3 adds project history and witness-ingestion documentation as mandatory maintenance files.

tei.title: TEI downloads
tei.summary: Downloadable TEI representing the current project data layers.
details: TEI structure is designed for the target architecture.
Witness TEI files for K/A1/A2/N/B are currently provisional reconstructions, not diplomatic transcriptions.
Future documentary witness TEI will use the ingestion contract and stable locus layer.

ingestion.title: Future witness ingestion
ingestion.summary: Prepared import path for transcriptions produced outside the system, including eScriptorium exports.
details: Preferred target inside the project is diplomatic TEI.
PAGE XML, ALTO XML, plain text, and direct TEI can enter through adapters.
Import and alignment are separate operations: first preserve the witness faithfully, then align it to canonical loci.
No real witness from the shared folders is ingested in version 2.3.

not-working.title: Functions not yet implemented
not-working.summary: Known future functions are documented rather than silently appearing incomplete.
details: Shared server-side persistence for research annotations is not implemented.
Documentary witness scans/transcriptions have not yet been ingested.
Final witness collation and a project-specific transmission hypothesis are not yet implemented.
The current entity/concept/distant-reading results should be regenerated when documentary texts arrive.
